```text
FINDING 1
  location: Remarks, first bullet
  severity: nonfatal
  claim:    "a Urysohn function is never unique"
  evidence: The unqualified statement is false.  Counterexample: let
            X = {0,1} with the discrete topology (metrizable, hence normal);
            take A = {0}, B = {1} (disjoint closed).  The only function
            f : X → [0,1] satisfying A ⊆ f⁻¹({0}) and B ⊆ f⁻¹({1}) is
            f(0)=0, f(1)=1, so the Urysohn function for this pair is unique.
            The remark therefore asserts a false universal claim.
```
